title: Cut generated commit subjects at a word boundary
summary: Replace the three bare `.chars().take(72)` cuts of generated subjects/titles (manage.rs, reading.rs, store.rs) with one shared word-boundary truncation helper, with tests and a CHANGELOG note. Audience: Athena maintainers reading git log.

defaults_applied.how: Helper unit tests plus subject/title tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
One shared helper replaces all three cut sites rather than fixing one.
Single focused change to truncation only.
Tests check outputs do not end mid-word.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: review finding n4 (mid-word cut like '…tells outsi'); audience is Athena maintainers reading git log and job titles.
The helper lives in athena-core (e.g. lib.rs) since all three sites are in that crate.
The take(60) at reading.rs:572 is unrelated and left alone.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests for the new helper pass under `cargo test`: over-limit text is cut at the last whitespace within 72 chars so no word is split; text at or under the limit is unchanged; a single over-long word is hard-cut at 72 chars; multibyte text does not panic.
A `cargo test` test builds a long intervention subject (manage.rs) and a long reading title (reading.rs) from multi-word text and shows neither ends mid-word and both are at most 72 chars.
The three `.chars().take(72)` sites (manage.rs subject, reading.rs title, store.rs title fallback) call the shared helper instead.
`cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check` and the full `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md notes that generated commit subjects and titles are cut at word boundaries.

out_of_scope: Other truncations (take(60), take(300), take(12)) that are not commit subjects or titles
